items.stem: Under the general measurement model, how is the profit expected from a group of insurance contracts recognised?

options.text: It is held as the contractual service margin and released to profit or loss as services are provided over the coverage period
options.rationale: Correct: the CSM defers unearned profit and is released over the coverage period.

options.text: It is recognised in full at the inception of the contract
options.rationale: Day-one profit is deferred in the CSM, not recognised immediately.

options.text: It is never recognised in profit or loss
options.rationale: The CSM is released to profit or loss over time.

options.text: It is recognised only when the contract matures or lapses
options.rationale: Profit is recognised as services are provided, not only at maturity.

items.explanation: Correct: the CSM defers unearned profit and is released over the coverage period.

items.stem: Which TWO building blocks form the fulfilment cash flows in the general measurement model? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Estimates of future cash flows adjusted for the time value of money (discounting)
options.rationale: Correct: discounted future cash-flow estimates are a building block.

options.text: A risk adjustment for non-financial risk
options.rationale: Correct: the risk adjustment for non-financial risk is a building block.

options.text: The insurer's targeted return on equity
options.rationale: A target return on equity is not a building block of fulfilment cash flows.

options.text: The market value of the insurer's own shares
options.rationale: The insurer's share price is irrelevant to the measurement.

items.explanation: Correct: discounted future cash-flow estimates are a building block.

items.stem: An insurer wants to recognise the entire first-year premium on a long-term policy as revenue immediately. Why is that generally inappropriate under IFRS 17?

options.text: Insurance revenue reflects services provided in the period and excludes investment components, so unearned profit is deferred rather than taken up front
options.rationale: Correct: revenue follows services provided, excluding investment components, with profit deferred in the CSM.

options.text: Premiums are never revenue under any circumstances
options.rationale: Premiums can generate insurance revenue, but recognised as services are provided.
There is no requirement to refund premiums.

options.text: Revenue can only be recognised at contract maturity
options.rationale: Revenue is recognised over the coverage period, not solely at maturity.

items.explanation: Correct: revenue follows services provided, excluding investment components, with profit deferred in the CSM.
